meta.title: SNOMED CT on MongoDB
meta.summary: Canonical SNOMED CT document storage with an optional term sidecar for terminology search and clinical note grounding.

whyMongoDB: SNOMED CT concepts are naturally document-shaped: each concept carries descriptions, language refsets, relationships, parents, ancestors, module metadata, and release metadata.
MongoDB can preserve the official JSON model as the canonical source while adding operational indexes for lookup, hierarchy traversal, and term retrieval.
The same persistence model runs on MongoDB Atlas and self-managed MongoDB. Atlas Search or vector search can be layered later, but the baseline strategy only requires MongoDB collections and indexes.
A separate term sidecar lets search and grounding evolve without rewriting the licensed canonical terminology payload.
primaryUseCases: Tenant-owned ingestion of licensed official SNOMED CT JSON releases.
Release inspection and diff before applying a new release.
Terminology search and navigation over descriptions, synonyms, parents, ancestors, and semantic tags.
Grounding clinical NLP mentions to candidate SNOMED CT concepts.
Benchmark retrieval support for clinical LLM extraction/grounding workflows.
nonGoalsForThisPack: It is not a SNOMED CT license manager.
It does not ship official SNOMED CT content.
It does not claim complete ECL grammar coverage in this first implementation.

canonical_concept.definition: One MongoDB document per SNOMED CT concept, preserving official IDs, descriptions, relationships, parents, ancestors, refsets, release metadata, and relationship attribute keys.

term_sidecar.definition: A derived collection with one document per searchable description/language. It supports lexical retrieval, grounding candidates, and LLM benchmark retrieval inputs.

release_diff.definition: A streamed comparison between the official JSON release and the active canonical MongoDB collection.

fixedByStrategy: Sidecar identity is releaseId + conceptId + descriptionId + languageCode.
Distribution credentials are not part of the runtime contract.
Distribution is not a runtime concern: customers obtain licensed JSON through official channels and place it in the configured local folder.
Default search is deterministic normalized lexical retrieval for MongoDB parity.

architectureNotes: The canonical collection is mandatory and supports lookup, hierarchy traversal, release diff, and basic ECL/subsumption queries.
The term sidecar is configurable but default-on. Search, grounding, and benchmark retrieval require it for production-quality behavior.
Release updates are streamed from JSON so large official files do not need to fit in memory.
